proposal.description: The PWM edge detector's delayed copy pwm_sync_d is cleared along with the windows and cp_delay while neither S_SS nor S_RUN is active, so entering S_SS while pwm_sync is already high produces a false cycle-boundary strobe.
proposal.reason: pwm_sync (Osc_sync) keeps toggling while the converter is idle. If S_SS is entered while it is high, pwm_rise fires on the first active clock and an extra (clear) sample goes into the soft-start window, which puts the window one cycle out of step. A faulted cycle then leaves the window one switching cycle early, so fault_count_ss_out and window_trip_SS fall one cycle sooner than they should.

proposal.description: The S_RUN window is written as a rotate instead of a shift, so the oldest sample leaving at bit WINDOW_RUN-1 comes back into bit 0 while the count still subtracts it.
proposal.reason: After a single faulted cycle in S_RUN, the faulted bit keeps going round the window, and the count loses one each time the bit passes the top. 16 cycles later fault_count_run_out is 0, and 16 cycles after that it wraps to 31, so window_trip goes high with no overcurrent present.

proposal.description: Copy-paste slip: the S_RUN count takes its leaving bit from the soft-start shift register, which is frozen during S_RUN, instead of from the run shift register.
proposal.reason: In S_RUN the subtracted bit is a constant from the soft-start history. If that bit is 0, faulted cycles are never taken off fault_count_run_out and the count builds up until window_trip asserts. If it is 1, the count drops on every cycle, wraps, and trips at once.

proposal.description: The S_RUN window stops sampling once window_trip has fired, so the count is held as evidence at the trip value instead of continuing to roll.
proposal.reason: Suppose the run count reaches trip_run while run_active stays high. fault_count_run_out then stays at that value and window_trip stays asserted, even after the overcurrent clears and the faulted cycles should have left the 16-cycle window.
